narr: West-northwesterly winds along a slowly-advancing warm frontal zone promoted the ample bulk shear and copious instability that produced numerous morning showers and thunderstorms. Storms tracked eastward along the I-74 corridor, producing isolated large hail, and later isolated wind damage and flash flooding. A road was washed-out in a possible microburst over northwestern Putnam County. All severe cells occurred over west-central Indiana.
ev: Thunderstorm heavy rains washed out an approximate 15-foot segment of County Road 900 West at about 1100 North, along and above drain pipes crossing under the road. Relayed by broadcast media via Twitter. Damage at Putnam-Parke County Line.
lsr: LATE REPORT OF AN APPROXIMATE 15 FOOT SEGMENT OF COUNTY ROAD 900 WEST AT ABOUT 1100 NORTH WASHED OUT ALONG AND ABOVE DRAIN PIPES CROSSING UNDER THE ROAD. TIME ESTIMATED FROM RADAR.
